lesson.title: Ik Onkar: The Oneness of God
lesson.subject: sikhi

contentBlocks.text: The Guru Granth Sahib opens with a single symbol that establishes the philosophical foundation for everything that follows: ੴ, Ik Onkar.

Ik Onkar means 'There is One God' or 'One Universal Creator' — a foundational philosophical claim of absolute oneness, not many separate gods, and not a God divided into competing parts. This isn't just a religious statement; it's a philosophical starting point with real implications: if all existence comes from one source, then all people, regardless of background, share that same fundamental origin — a philosophical basis for the equality you've studied in earlier grades through Langar and the Khalsa. Think about how believing 'we all come from one common source' might philosophically support a value like human equality, in a way that's more than just a nice sentiment.
You just examined how a foundational philosophical claim (oneness) connects logically to a real ethical value (equality). Tomorrow we'll go deeper into Naam, the concept of the Divine Name.

objectives: Explain Ik Onkar as the foundational philosophical claim of absolute oneness
Connect this philosophical claim to the ethical value of equality studied in earlier grades
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Introduce Ik Onkar as the Guru Granth Sahib's opening philosophical statement.
2. Discuss what 'absolute oneness' means as a philosophical claim, not just a religious one.
3. Connect this to equality (Langar, Khalsa) from earlier grades, discussing the logical link.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's topic: Naam.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on the simple statement 'there is one God, so we all come from the same source' without requiring the deeper philosophical implications yet
Ready for more: ask them to compare this oneness concept to a philosophical or religious idea from a different tradition they may know about
Text-only content, per the platform's content policy — no depiction of any Guru, symbolic references only
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. Ik Onkar means 'there is one God' or 'one universal creator.' 2. This is a philosophical claim of absolute oneness. 3. If all existence shares one source, this provides a philosophical basis for human equality.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Introduces the course's 'Sikh philosophy' description with its most foundational concept, explicitly connecting abstract philosophy to concrete ethical values (equality) already studied in earlier grades.
